title: Quantitative persistence in a fixed-city area equation
description:
For every fixed finite collection of at least two distinct interior sites in the unit square and every strictly positive initial probability vector, consider the hard weighted-Voronoi area equation z_i prime = A_i(z) - z_i, where city i maximizes z_i^alpha times distance to the power -beta. We give a quantitative all-coordinate persistence theorem when beta > 2 alpha: an explicit time-dependent lower bound, a positive bound for all time, and a positive limiting inferior bound independent of the starting state. An asymmetric three-city instance with alpha=2, beta=8 has every share between 1/4096 and 2047/2048 for all nonnegative time. This refutes the unrestricted alpha > 1 collapse alternative in the literal 2007 Conjecture 32(a) and the catalog conjunction containing it. The result does not establish convergence, equilibrium uniqueness, initial-value independence of a limit, or stochastic city-founding conclusions. Zero initial weights, coincident sites, boundary sites, and the one-city case are outside the stated theorem.

The model and conjecture are Aldous's. Multiplicatively weighted Voronoi/Apollonius geometry is classical; the original 2007 notes already contain the protected-neighborhood mechanism and area exponent 2 alpha / beta in an unfinished stochastic argument. The scalar substitution and integrating-factor step are standard. Ferudun's unrefereed preprint, stated release 14 October 2026, explicitly gives robust two-city Conjecture 32(a) counterexamples in another parameter range and records the ratio-invariance inconsistency. Its proved every-exponent derivative lemma and position continuity also imply qualitative two-city noncollapse in the present beta > 2 alpha regime. These overlapping conclusions receive direct credit. The present theorem supplies all-site, all-positive-initial-state quantitative persistence; it is not advertised as the first negative answer or as a new geometric method. The original complete PR was recorded on 6 October 2026, but chronology and bounded searches certify neither firstness, exhaustive novelty nor worldwide current openness.

The deposit contains a five-page research note and a verification archive with editable source, all forty frozen original files, original nested evidence archives, independent analytical and bounded priority audit evidence, source version/hash locators, an externally pinned closed-inventory verifier and deterministic ZIP builder. Default finite replay runs the original witness/checker self-tests under normal and optimized Python. Optional full provenance requires three complete pinned corpora and two separately supplied primary PDFs. Primary publications, extracted source text, page images, raw dataset records and private credentials are excluded. Artifact hashes and finite checks do not certify the analytic theorem or priority. Compressed-byte reproducibility is limited to identical inputs and the same Python ZIP implementation and zlib runtime.

OpenAI tools were used extensively in solving, proof development, drafting, coding, reproduction and adversarial checking. This is an unrefereed preprint; no completed external human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification is claimed. The author is responsible for the claims.
